mentl/0693bf4:
Seven bypass sites sat behind one unknown: does a handler's extent survive
a self-tail-calling loop? `mentl space` needs it, because its accept loop
never returns, and guessing inside a sweep is how a wrong answer gets
canonized.

tests/micros/mn-handler-extent-tail-loop.mn asks directly — install
outside, perform inside every iteration — and answers 10. The extent
survives, and the handler's state accumulates across iterations (bump
answers 1, 2, 3, 4), which is the half a server actually depends on.

So space_run installs ~> wasi_filesystem over space_loop and the file
server performs fs_exists / fs_read_file. The install immediately made the
medium refuse space_conn and space_loop for declaring Memory + Alloc +
WASI while performing Filesystem. That refusal is the proof the bypass had
been suppressing; both signatures carry + Filesystem now.

driver_warm_persist's mkdir converted too — its row had declared
Filesystem all along and only the call site lagged.

persist_write was converted and reverted by the board, which is the
sharper finding. It declares Memory + Alloc + Filesystem + WASI while
`mentl query "type persist_write"` reported the inferred row as Alloc +
Memory + WASI — the bypass had made that signature false in the other
direction, over-declaring a capability the body never reached. Converting
looked obviously right and the frontier's persist shadow leg refused it:
fs_write_file answers E_MissingVariable in that subset link, because the
Filesystem effect is declared in src/types.mn and lib/persist.mn must
compile standalone. A lib/ module cannot perform this effect, so the impl
there is forced rather than lazy — a floor under the ratchet, not a site
awaiting work.

mentl/062e66a:
Ultracode design pass on the graph-is-the-machine native backend: ten
layers designed to the metal from the kernel, each adversarially
refuted for foreign-fluency / deferrals / breaks / does-it-hit-silicon,
then a completeness critic across all ten. The refutations converged
unanimously on one correction (N proposals to one attractor = the
truth signal, PLAN §7): the addressing/projection substrate
(graph-image, handle-as-offset, eight-aspect projection,
assembler-as-handler) is right; the 'no stack, every frame a never-freed
image record' spine is SML/NJ heap-CPS without its GC and its own hot
path falsifies it.

The correction, derivable today from verified artifacts: frame
representation IS the resume-cardinality/ownership grade (this session's
landing) — OneShot activations are trail-reclaimed image frames
(graph.mn's graph_rollback is the activation spine, not %rsp), MultiShot
captures the delimited frame segment as a memcpy-able record; so
'continuation = memcpy' is finally true, loops stay bounded with no GC,
and !Outside holds because reclamation is the kernel's own trail.

docs/NATIVE.md carries the corrected design, the two keystones
(cardinality->frame-rep + trail; deterministic handle partition), the
four systemic drifts killed once, the missing concerns the critique
surfaced (FP determinism as the silent fixpoint-killer, foreign interop,
self-hosting the encoder), and the S0-S18 build spine — WASM-peer-
verifiable through S12, native first-light at S13. Band N updated with
the keystones and the WASM multi-shot peers (S3/S4 in the peer, proven
this session).

A stranger's packet no longer kills the app. The reachable panic was not

ggrs's Message layout, vets the RLE stream with checked bounds, walks the
frames the way ggrs will, and refuses anything not exactly one

bytes it emits must decode as a real ggrs::Message or the guard is
inert. One upstream assert on start_frame remains open and is not
closable at this boundary; documented, not hidden.

perennials/064ad46:
The guide said "nobody recorded it", and we cannot know that. Somebody has
almost certainly measured this plant's bloom colour somewhere; all we know
is that the three sources we pull didn't hand it to us, or that the
transform didn't take it. The old phrasing made a claim about the world out
of a fact about our pipeline.

So every absence is now scoped to us: "not in our sources", "not in our
data", "our sources don't say". The rule it serves is unchanged and the
reason is the same one it always was, that a blank is not a no.

CLAUDE.md documented the old wording verbatim as the governing rule, so it
was wrong the moment this landed; it names the subtler trap now.

This also carries BloomCalendar's share of the "Mark blooming today"
rename, which the previous commit left stale in a comment.

stoop/06d9af6:
The intake dithers every photograph down to two tones and then handed the
canvas to the browser's own PNG encoder, which writes whatever the canvas
holds: 32-bit RGBA. A 1000-pixel photograph cost 486 KB as a data URL instead
of the 83 KB the same black and white needs at one bit per pixel. Because an
exported issue carries its photographs inline, that surcharge was not paid
once but again in every file anyone handed to anyone. An eight-page issue with
a photograph on every page was 4.0 MB and is now 798 KB. The pixels are
identical; the two tone counts match exactly before and after. pdfAddImage has
always packed these bits properly on the way to the printer, so this is only
the screen's copy catching up with the paper's.

The size ceiling in check.sh went with it, because it was the thing that hid
this. It asserted that the press stays a minority of the payload it rides in
and that an issue with a few photographs runs 200 to 500 KB, and failed the
build at 256 KB on the app fragment. None of that had been measured. The press
was 95 percent of a text-only issue and 22 percent of a six-photograph one,
and the fragment was the one term in the sum that barely moves, while the term
that mattered was six times larger than it needed to be and unwatched.

What replaces it is measured rather than asserted. test/08-weight.js publishes
a real issue and weighs it: a full eight-page issue stays under a megabyte, a
photograph under 120 KB, and every stored PNG reports bit depth 1 greyscale in
its own header, which is the one bound here resting on a principle instead of
a round number. check.sh keeps a cheap ratchet on the fixed cost, since it has
no browser and cannot build an issue, and now says that is what it is rather
than dressing a policy choice as a derived limit. FORMAT.md specifies the
encoding so the next implementation does not rediscover it the same way.
